sections.h2: Who values and collects property tax in Jefferson County, KY?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work in Jefferson County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's value, and the Sheriff's Office bills and collects the tax. The Sheriff says it brings in about $1 billion a year from more than 300,000 taxpayers on behalf of 13 taxing jurisdictions.

The PVA sits in the Glassworks Building at 815 W. Market St., Suite 400, Louisville, KY 40202, phone (502) 574-6380. The Sheriff's Property Tax Department is in the Fiscal Court Building at 700 W. Liberty St., phone (502) 574-5479, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM.

Values reflect the property's fair cash value on January 1. Tax bills go to the owner of record on that date, or to the current owner if the PVA's records had been updated by the time the roll was printed.

sections.h2: When are Jefferson County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed by November 1, and the 2 percent discount in Jefferson County runs through December 1, a month past the November 1 date in the state statute. The Sheriff's schedule gives each stage a date range.

Jefferson County Sheriff payment schedule for current-year bills (source: Jefferson County Sheriff's Office)
DatesWhat you pay
November 1 to December 1Bill less 2 percent
December 2 to January 4Face amount
January 5 to February 5Face amount plus 5 percent
February 6 to April 15Face amount plus 10 percent penalty and 10 percent Sheriff's add-on fee

If a date lands on a weekend or a Sheriff's Office holiday, it moves to the next regular business day. Failing to receive a bill does not waive the penalty, so call the Property Tax Department in the second week of November if nothing has arrived.

  • Pay in person with cash, check or money order, using the payment stub.
  • Mail checks to Jefferson County Sheriff, PO Box 34570, Louisville, KY 40232-4570.
  • Use the online portal. An eCheck costs $2, and cards cost 2.25 percent, with a flat $1.95 on payments of $86 or less.
  • Drop an envelope in the Sheriff's dropbox at the downtown office or at a County Clerk branch such as Dixie, Fairdale, Highview, East or Westport.

The Sheriff also accepts partial payments on current-year bills during the collection period.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jefferson County property assessment?
sections.html:
You start with the PVA, not the board. State law in KRS 133.120 requires a conference with the PVA during the annual open inspection period, and Jefferson County runs that conference online.

  • Submit a separate online conference for each parcel ID you dispute.
  • Upload support such as an appraisal, photos, an insurance policy, repair estimates, construction costs or a listing contract.
  • Use sales from roughly the last two years that match your property in size and type. The PVA's sales search is free to the public during the appeal window.
  • Expect a conference result by mail or email about 5 to 10 business days after the PVA gets your submission.

If you still disagree, sign the bottom section of the result form and file it with the Jefferson County Clerk. The deadline is one workday after the inspection period ends. The Local Board of Assessment Appeals hears the case, and an owner who skips the board cannot go straight to the Board of Tax Appeals. A paid representative must be a listed professional with written authorization from you.

An appeal does not pause your bill. You owe tax on the value you claim, with any added tax and interest billed later if the board sets a higher figure.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption for Jefferson County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The Department of Revenue resets that figure every two years.

Against the Census median home value of $248,400, the taxable base would fall to $199,300. The exemption lowers the bill but cannot erase it unless the home's assessment is below the exemption amount. Apply through the Jefferson County PVA. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport, and disability must come from a federal or retirement-system program.

A separate West End program run by LHOME and the West End Opportunity Partnership offers a grant or 0 percent loan to qualifying residents of nine neighborhoods: Algonquin, California, Chickasaw, Park DuValle, Parkhill, Parkland, Portland, Russell and Shawnee. Call LHOME at (502) 882-8091 to ask about eligibility.

sections.h2: Do Jefferson County home rule cities send a second tax bill?
sections.html:
Many do. The Sheriff's bill covers the state, Louisville Metro, the school board and fire districts, but smaller cities inside the county issue and collect their own bills on top of it.

The PVA counts 83 incorporated taxing jurisdictions among about 60,000 properties. Those cities run their own police, fire, sanitation or parks, and each posts its own rates. Since 2015, Kentucky has used two city classes: first class, meaning Louisville, and home rule cities, which covers all others.

If your house is in a small city such as St. Matthews or Jeffersontown, ask that city's office for its bill and payoff figure as well. Sellers who check only the Sheriff's account can miss a city balance.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Jefferson County tax when I sell the house?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property and the owner. State law treats it as the taxpayer's personal debt from the January 1 assessment date, and the lien under KRS 134.420 lasts up to 11 years whoever owns the parcel.

After April 15 the unpaid bill goes to the County Clerk. Interest of 1 percent per month and further fees begin there, and the bill can be bought by a third party at the clerk's summer sale. The County Attorney's page puts the extra costs near 40 percent once a certificate of delinquency exists.

Taxes on a payment plan with the County Attorney cannot be sold at that sale, and plans for a given year open after the Sheriff's collection ends. Waiver requests for certain penalties go in writing to the same office.

At closing, the Sheriff notes that the seller usually pays a prorated share for the part of the year they owned the home, and the buyer then pays the whole bill when it arrives. Read the settlement statement to see how your closing agent split it.

sections.h2: What is Jefferson County, Kentucky, like for a property tax payer?
sections.html:
Jefferson County is the state's most populous county, with 795,222 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, and it shares its boundaries with Louisville Metro. Its land area is 380.8 square miles, with about 2,056 residents per square mile in 2020.

  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $248,400.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 62.1 percent.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,593, and $608 without one.
  • Median household income: $69,866.
  • Housing units, 2025: 366,702.

Public schools come from Jefferson County Public Schools and the Anchorage Independent district, a K through 8 system. Recording and transfer questions go to the County Clerk's Legal Records Division.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jefferson County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office at 700 W. Liberty St., Louisville, online, by mail to PO Box 34570, or in a dropbox. The office is open weekdays from 8 AM to 4 PM and accepts cash, checks and money orders in person.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: The discount is 2 percent for payments made from November 1 through December 1. After that, the face amount applies until January 4, and penalties begin on January 5.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Jefferson County bill in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, during the Sheriff's collection period. The Sheriff accepts partial payments on current-year bills between November 1 and April 15. After April 15, the County Attorney decides who qualifies for a plan on delinquent bills.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Jefferson County assessment?
faqs.a: File an online conference with the Jefferson County PVA during the open inspection period, then appeal through the County Clerk to the Local Board of Assessment Appeals if the result stands. Do this before bills go out, because you cannot contest value from the tax bill itself.

faqs.q: Does a home sale clear the property tax lien?
faqs.a: No. Delinquent tax stays a lien on the parcel, and the title company will want it paid from proceeds. Ask the Sheriff for current-year figures and the County Clerk for any older certificate before you list.
